purpose: Review the 2016 Batanes NSAP fishery assessment as historical, gear- and landing-dependent evidence; preserve its 15 named dominant catch labels without interpreting the aggregate 580-species claim as a transcribed checklist or creating site-level occurrences.

source.title: Municipal Marine Fisheries Assessment of Batanes Island, Philippines (2009-2013)
source.publisher: Kuroshio Science; University of Kochi Repository
source.citation: Morales, M. C., Encarnacion, A. B., & Calicdan, M. A. (2016). Municipal Marine Fisheries Assessment of Batanes Island, Philippines (2009-2013). Kuroshio Science, 10-1, 7-22.
source.access: Full article text reviewed from the university-repository PDF. A PDF screenshot request was throttled; no local PDF copy was retained and no image-based Table 2 transcription was completed.
source.license: No item-specific reuse license or copyright terms verified in the reviewed article text or repository result.

study.setting: Historical municipal marine-fishery assessment using National Stock Assessment Program (NSAP) landing-center data; not an all-habitat biodiversity survey.
study.studyPeriod: January 2009 through December 2013; elsewhere the article calls this a six-year period, an internal duration inconsistency.
study.methodsAsReported: The article describes standard NSAP collection at six landing centers, catch sampling from fish holds/tubs/styrofoam, sorting and weighing by species, and forms submitted to BFAR Region 02. It says sampling was conducted every other two days; that interval wording is retained as reported and not normalized.
samplingFieldsAsReported: catch and effort per fishing operation
spatialLimits: The named sites locate landing centers, not the capture position of each fish or taxon.
Although the methods say fishing-ground information was collected, the reviewed article does not publish a taxon-by-capture-ground or taxon-by-landing-site event matrix.
The overview map is not a verified coordinate table; no site coordinates or fishing-ground geometry were derived.

aggregateCatchComposition.articleWording: The article reports 580 species and 66 families for the study period.
aggregateCatchComposition.interpretationLimit: The full set of names was not transcribed. The definition of the aggregate's taxonomic scope is not reconciled in the article text with its separately reported vertebrate, invertebrate, and elasmobranch catch shares; do not present 580 as a verified fish-only checklist size.

reportedFindings.seasonalityAsReported: The paper describes a March-May peak for the top fifteen taxa overall, with differing patterns by taxon. These are 2009-2013 catch-season summaries, not current seasonal presence or fishing advice.
reportedFindings.dolphinfishDietLead: The article says flying fishes are a favored prey of Coryphaena hippurus but attributes the stomach-content figure to Rose (1966) cited through Palko et al. (1982). This is a secondary citation chain in this assessment, not a diet sample conducted by the Batanes study.
reportedFindings.stockMetricConflict: The abstract's stated exploitation values for Tylosurus crocodilus and Cheilopogon unicolor do not align cleanly with the E and Emax rows in Table 8. Numeric stock-status labels are held pending table-image review and interpretation.

qualityAndReuseLimits: This is fishery-dependent catch evidence, selected by gear, landing-center sampling, and commercial importance; it is not a complete provincial species checklist or a direct census of fish communities.

The article reports 580 species, but the complete name set is not reproduced in this review. The parsed PDF exposes the Table 2 heading without extractable rows, and screenshot retrieval was throttled; visually inspect the table before any full-list claim or transcription.

Cheilopogon spilinopterus is retained as the article's verbatim scientific label. Its spelling and identity are unresolved; its published common name also duplicates the common name used for Cheilopogon furcatus, and it shares the printed local name Dibang with Cheilopogon nigricans.
The abstract and Table 8 appear to conflate exploitation E and Emax for some taxa. Do not use the abstract's numeric stock claims as current conservation status or management advice.
The study gives no specimen-voucher identifiers or taxon-to-capture-location matrix in the reviewed text; no species-level occurrence rows, coordinates, or geometry were created.

No item-specific license was verified. Repository accessibility is not treated as permission to reproduce or adapt the article's table, maps, or figures. No source table, figure, map, or PDF was copied.
The stated dolphinfish prey relation is cited through older literature and requires direct-source review before use in a diet feature.
Historical catches, seasonal peaks, gear contributions, and mortality estimates are not current presence, catchability, legal, safety, or bait guidance.

relatedSourceComparison.note: The separate Villarao et al. 2026 source analyzes 2014-2023 NSAP landings for Coryphaena hippurus at 19 sites. The periods and scopes differ; do not sum catch amounts or treat landing centers as capture grounds.

nextAction: Visually inspect Table 2 when the repository PDF can be rendered, then record only source-verbatim names with independent taxonomy checks and keep the article's name list separate from occurrence data. Verify the Cheilopogon spilinopterus label and the cited Rose/Palko diet source before reusing either claim.
